paragraphs: When a diffusion model trains on images generated by an earlier model, repeated cycles can gradually damage its output. This paper studies that process through the distinction between generalization and memorization: producing new content versus increasingly reproducing examples from the training data. That perspective connects model collapse to a recognizable change in what the generator actually creates.

The authors identify declining entropy in the synthetic training data as the direct driver of this transition. Entropy here captures the diversity or uncertainty present in the data. As successive synthetic datasets lose that richness, the models move toward memorization. The paper therefore treats entropy as an indicator of degradation and as a basis for deciding which generated examples to retain.

The proposed intervention selects training data using entropy. In the reported experiments, this improves both visual quality and diversity during recursive generation and effectively prevents collapse. The findings support managing the composition of synthetic training data as a way to preserve generation quality across repeated training cycles.
neurips-2025-a-closer-look-at-model-coll.tldr: The paper links diffusion-model collapse to declining synthetic-data entropy and uses entropy-based data selection to preserve quality and diversity.

paragraphs: Link prediction asks which connections are missing or likely to form in a network. This paper addresses the version that uses only the pattern of existing connections. Its starting point is Cannistraci-Hebb theory, which describes link formation through local communities and favors communities with fewer connections leading outside them.

The theory defines those communities using paths between nodes. Paths of length two represent interactions associated with similarity, while paths of length three represent interactions associated with complementary or diverse roles. The proposed Cannistraci-Hebb Adaptive system automatically chooses both a rule from this theory and a path length for each network. This allows the explanation of connectivity to adapt to the network being modeled.

Across 1,269 networks spanning 14 domains, the authors report consistently better link prediction than the compared statistical, embedding, and message-passing neural approaches. They also report insights into mechanisms of link formation. The contribution combines empirical adaptability with interpretable structural rules, so the selected model describes how local connectivity supports its predictions.
neurips-2025-adaptive-cannistraci-hebb-n.tldr: CHA adapts interpretable network rules and path lengths to predict missing links, outperforming the compared methods across 1,269 networks.

paragraphs: Building an agent system involves choosing tools, models, and other agents that work well together within a budget. Searching their written descriptions can be unreliable because descriptions may omit capabilities and do not directly establish present usefulness. This paper treats component selection as an optimization problem involving performance, cost, and compatibility.

Its composer agent uses an approach inspired by the knapsack problem: assemble a valuable collection while respecting resource constraints. The composer actively tests candidates and updates estimates of their utility during selection. This makes observed capabilities part of the decision, providing a structured way to reuse existing components as task requirements and budgets vary.

Evaluations using Claude 3.5 Sonnet on five datasets place the composer consistently on the reported performance–cost Pareto frontier. Single-agent success improves by up to 31.6% relative to retrieval baselines. In a multi-agent setting with more than 100 available agents, success rises from 37% to 87%. These findings support testing and budget-aware selection as useful ingredients in automated agent assembly.
neurips-2025-automated-composition-of-ag.tldr: A knapsack-inspired composer tests and selects agent components to improve task success while controlling component costs.

paragraphs: Some medical decision problems involve events that recur in an alternating pattern, making a single final survival time an incomplete description of the outcome. This paper develops reinforcement learning for that structure. Its objective is to increase the probability that the interval between consecutive events exceeds a threshold considered clinically meaningful.

That objective changes what the learning algorithm rewards. Maximizing an average duration does not directly express the chance of clearing a particular threshold. The authors identify a lower bound on the desired probability and use it to obtain an objective consisting of accumulated log probabilities. This reformulation lets standard reinforcement learning algorithms optimize a bound connected to the original clinical objective.

The paper establishes theoretical properties of the resulting optimal policy and evaluates the algorithm numerically. In those experiments, it produces a higher probability of event intervals exceeding the chosen threshold than the compared existing methods. The stated evidence therefore supports a probability-focused decision framework for recurrent events, with its optimization built around the derived lower bound.
neurips-2025-beyond-average-value-functi.tldr: This reinforcement learning framework targets the probability of sufficiently long gaps between recurrent events through a tractable lower-bound objective.

paragraphs: An audio caption can sound plausible while describing something absent from the recording. Evaluating that alignment is especially difficult when no trusted reference caption exists. BRACE is a benchmark for testing whether automatic evaluation methods can judge how well a caption matches audio under these conditions.

The benchmark separates two challenges. BRACE-Main tests fine-grained comparisons between captions, while BRACE-Hallucination targets subtle invented content. Its construction combines quality filtering, language-model-generated corruptions, and human annotation. The main purpose is to evaluate caption-scoring metrics, although the same benchmark can also assess how well large audio language models connect sound with language.

The authors test CLAPScore with multiple underlying CLAP models and evaluate several large audio language models. On BRACE-Main, the strongest CLAP-based metric reaches an F1 score of 70.01, while the strongest tested audio language model reaches 63.19. These results expose weaknesses in the evaluated approaches and establish a concrete resource for studying more reliable judgments of audio-caption alignment.
neurips-2025-brace-a-benchmark-for-robus.tldr: BRACE tests reference-free audio-caption evaluation and reveals weaknesses in detecting fine-grained mismatches and hallucinated content.

paragraphs: Discovering which parts of a changing system causally influence others is difficult when researchers cannot intervene directly. Existing methods and benchmarks often emphasize relatively small, deterministic systems with weak nonlinear behavior. CausalDynamics broadens the testing environment for recovering causal structure from observations of systems evolving over time.

The benchmark provides known causal graphs from thousands of systems built with coupled differential equations. These include linear and nonlinear interactions, ordinary and stochastic equations, and two idealized climate models. Because the generating structure is available, algorithms can be evaluated against the intended causal connections while facing noisy observations, confounding, and delayed effects.

The authors use this collection to evaluate existing causal discovery algorithms and provide an extensible workflow for constructing additional coupled systems. Its modular design lets users build hierarchies of physical systems for different challenges. The contribution is a broader evaluation and data-generation foundation; the abstract presents more robust, widely applicable causal discovery as a goal the framework can help advance.
neurips-2025-causaldynamics-a-largescale.tldr: CausalDynamics benchmarks causal graph discovery across thousands of dynamical systems with nonlinear, noisy, confounded, and delayed interactions.

paragraphs: A language model can drift between topics, but that behavior need not follow the same dynamics as spontaneous human thought. This paper studies topic changes in next-token prediction, using a mathematical definition of a topic based on collections of Token Priority Graphs. The definition makes token ordering central to the analysis.

For a simplified single-layer self-attention model under suitable conditions, the authors show that the priority ordering of tokens associated with the input topic is maintained. They also establish a necessary condition for spontaneous topic change: lower-priority tokens must outnumber all higher-priority tokens of that topic. Meeting this count condition is not stated to guarantee a change.

The theory further finds that longer contexts and more ambiguous input topics do not increase the likelihood of spontaneous change in the studied setting. Experiments with modern language models support the reported effects of context length and ambiguity. Together, these findings identify a specific divergence from human spontaneous thought while keeping the formal guarantees tied to the simplified model and its conditions.
neurips-2025-dynamics-of-spontaneous-top.tldr: Theory and experiments identify constraints on spontaneous topic changes in self-attention models that differ from patterns of human thought.

paragraphs: Vision-language-action models connect visual observations and language with robot actions, but their computational and memory demands can hinder deployment. This paper introduces VLA-Pruner, a framework that accelerates inference without additional training. Its central idea is to address redundancy across the language, visual, and action-generation parts of the model together.

The language module loses layers identified as functionally inconsequential through analysis of similarities between layers. The visual pathway retains a smaller, diverse set of tokens chosen to balance task relevance with coverage of the available information. In the diffusion-based action head, intermediate features are cached and reused to reduce repeated computation across successive generation steps.

Applied to CogACT, the framework delivers a 1.93-fold inference speedup and reduces floating-point operations to 28.9% of the original amount. The reported success-rate decrease on SIMPLER is 0.6%. These results demonstrate a favorable efficiency–performance tradeoff in the evaluated model and benchmark, showing the value of coordinating reductions across several sources of computational redundancy.
neurips-2025-efficientvla-training-free-.tldr: VLA-Pruner accelerates CogACT without retraining by removing redundant language layers, visual tokens, and diffusion computations.

paragraphs: The law of supply and demand describes prices moving toward a level where supply and demand balance in a perfectly competitive market. This paper asks how that collective outcome can arise from the behavior of individual sellers. It approaches the question through online learning, where decisions are revised over repeated interactions.

Each seller chooses its own selling price to maximize its individual revenue. The central assumption is that every seller uses a no-swap regret algorithm. This learning criterion concerns whether consistently replacing chosen actions with other actions would have improved past performance. It provides a precise condition on how sellers adapt their pricing decisions over time.

Under that condition, the authors show that the collective pricing dynamics converge to the market-clearing price. The result gives a mathematical connection between individual revenue-seeking learning and market-level balance. Its significance is the emergence of coordinated pricing behavior from separate adaptive decisions, with convergence tied specifically to the stated learning rule and competitive-market setting.
neurips-2025-explaining-the-law-of-suppl.tldr: The paper shows that sellers using no-swap regret pricing algorithms collectively converge to a market-clearing price in its competitive-market setting.

paragraphs: Online reinforcement learning must balance trying uncertain actions with exploiting actions already believed to work well. This becomes challenging when values and policies use complex function approximations. The paper develops an actor-critic method that connects a practical optimization objective with theoretical guarantees about the cost of learning through interaction.

The authors reinterpret optimism through primal-dual optimization and derive value-incentivized actor-critic, or VAC. Its single objective favors estimates that both fit collected state transitions and imply higher values. This combines the pressure to remain consistent with observed experience and the incentive to pursue promising possibilities within one optimization problem.

For linear Markov decision processes, VAC receives near-optimal regret guarantees in both finite-horizon and infinite-horizon settings. Regret expresses the accumulated performance shortfall while learning, so these results characterize how efficiently exploration can proceed. The authors also extend the analysis to general function approximation under appropriate assumptions. Those qualifications matter: the abstract does not claim unconditional guarantees for arbitrary neural network implementations.
neurips-2025-exploration-from-a-primal-d.tldr: VAC combines data consistency and optimistic value estimates in one actor-critic objective, with near-optimal regret guarantees for linear MDPs.

paragraphs: Flow-GRPO brings online policy-gradient reinforcement learning to flow matching models. The challenge addressed by its first mechanism is that a deterministic generation process does not directly provide the stochastic exploration used by reinforcement learning. The method converts the model's ordinary differential equation into a stochastic differential equation while preserving its marginal distribution at every timestep.

A second mechanism reduces the number of denoising steps used during training while keeping the original inference-step count. The authors report that this makes sampling more efficient without sacrificing performance. Together, the mechanisms make it possible to explore different generation outcomes and use reward feedback to update the model more efficiently.

In text-to-image experiments with SD3.5-M, GenEval accuracy rises from 63% to 95%, alongside stronger object counting, spatial relations, and attribute generation. Visual text-rendering accuracy rises from 59% to 92%, and human-preference alignment also improves. The experiments show very little reward hacking: higher rewards generally avoid appreciable losses in image quality or diversity in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-flow-grpo-training-flow-mat.tldr: Flow-GRPO enables online reinforcement learning for flow matching and substantially improves the reported text-to-image generation results.

paragraphs: Temporal signals contain information that persists over different durations. HetSyn gives individual synapses in a spiking neural network their own time constants, allowing connections to retain and integrate information at different rates. This draws on the diversity of synaptic behavior observed in biological neurons.

The framework places temporal integration in synaptic currents and implements the idea through HetSynLIF, an extension of the leaky integrate-and-fire neuron. Different parameter configurations recover conventional LIF neurons, threshold-adapting neurons, and models with variation at the neuron level. This makes the proposal a general framework that contains several existing neuron designs as particular configurations.

The authors report improved performance on pattern generation, delayed matching, speech recognition, and visual recognition tasks. They also observe noise robustness, stronger working memory, effectiveness with limited numbers of neurons, and generalization across timescales. Learned time constants show trends consistent with biological observations. These findings support synapse-level temporal diversity as a useful ingredient for processing signals whose relevant information unfolds at multiple speeds.
neurips-2025-hetsyn-versatile-timescale-.tldr: HetSyn assigns distinct temporal dynamics to individual synapses, improving reported spiking-network performance, memory, and robustness across tasks.

paragraphs: Symbolic regression searches for mathematical expressions that explain data or satisfy another objective while remaining concise and interpretable. The number of possible expressions makes this a difficult combinatorial search. This paper improves Monte Carlo Tree Search by changing both how search effort is allocated and how the algorithm moves between candidate expressions.

The first change is an extreme bandit allocation strategy aimed at discovering globally optimal expressions. Its finite-time guarantees depend on assumptions about polynomial reward decay. The second introduces mutation and crossover as state-jumping actions, allowing movement to promising regions without constructing every expression through a strictly sequential series of symbol choices.

These jumps also change the reward landscape encountered during search, which the authors associate with improved robustness and efficiency. Numerical studies examine the contributions of the changes and compare the method on datasets with known underlying expressions and black-box datasets. Recovery rates are competitive with leading libraries, and the method achieves favorable tradeoffs between fitting accuracy and expression complexity.
neurips-2025-improving-monte-carlo-tree-.tldr: The method improves symbolic-regression tree search with specialized search allocation and mutation- and crossover-based jumps between expressions.

paragraphs: A single multi-agent policy can struggle across tasks whose best actions differ substantially. This paper observes that the dynamics behind tasks can have a more useful pattern of similarity: some task groups share closely related behavior, while unrelated groups differ considerably. M3W uses that structure to organize a model of how the environment evolves.

The method places mixture-of-experts components inside a world model. A SoftMoE dynamics model and a SparseMoE predictor support reuse among related tasks while avoiding conflicting learning signals across dissimilar ones. For planning, M3W predicts possible future rollouts and evaluates and optimizes actions through those predictions, without directly depending on an explicit policy model.

The authors evaluate the approach on 14 Bi-DexHands tasks and 24 MA-Mujoco tasks, reporting superior performance, sample efficiency, and adaptability across tasks. The contribution is a modular approach to shared environmental prediction and planning. Its motivation rests on the observed grouping of dynamics, making task similarity a basis for deciding where knowledge should be shared.
neurips-2025-learning-and-planning-multi.tldr: M3W uses a mixture-of-experts world model to share dynamics knowledge across related multi-agent tasks and plan actions through predicted rollouts.

paragraphs: Neural network learning commonly focuses on adjusting connection weights. This paper shifts the learning target to plasticity: the rules that determine how those connections change. Its Plasticity-Driven Learning Framework applies that idea to spiking neural networks, taking inspiration from the brain's capacity to adapt through changing synaptic behavior.

The framework reworks functional and presynaptic-dependent forms of plasticity around this objective. Learning a rule for synaptic change gives the network a mechanism for dynamic adaptation, rather than making the learned connection values the sole outcome of training. The central design question becomes how connections should evolve as the network encounters changing demands.

The authors report improvements in working memory, multitasking, and adaptability in complex real-world scenarios. They also describe relationships between different forms of plasticity and cognitive functions. These findings position learned plasticity as a route toward more adaptable spiking networks and as a way to investigate how mechanisms of synaptic change relate to particular abilities associated with biological learning.
neurips-2025-learning-the-plasticity-pla.tldr: The framework learns rules for changing synapses in spiking networks, with reported improvements in memory, multitasking, and adaptation.

paragraphs: Mobile agents must often complete long sequences of screen interactions while handling unfamiliar interfaces and recovering from mistakes. MobileUse addresses these challenges with a graphical-interface agent built around monitoring its own progress. Its design treats recovery and environmental understanding as central parts of executing a user's instructions.

The agent reflects at several timescales, from checking individual actions to assessing progress toward the overall task. Reflection-on-Demand controls when this additional checking is used, aiming to preserve efficiency. A proactive exploration module separately plans exploratory interactions to improve the agent's understanding of an unfamiliar environment before that lack of knowledge undermines execution.

MobileUse achieves reported success rates of 62.9% on AndroidWorld and 44.2% on AndroidLab, establishing new state-of-the-art performance in those evaluations. The authors also release a toolkit for automated operation of physical mobile devices. The findings support combining selective self-monitoring with planned exploration to improve mobile task execution, particularly where errors and uncertainty accumulate over a sequence of actions.
neurips-2025-mobileuse-a-hierarchical-re.tldr: MobileUse combines reflection across multiple timescales with proactive exploration to improve mobile task completion and error recovery.

paragraphs: This paper studies online convex optimization when decisions lie in an lp-ball with p greater than two. Performance is measured by regret, the accumulated shortfall against a comparison decision. Although optimal regret remains sublinear, its behavior changes depending on whether the number of dimensions exceeds the number of interaction rounds.

The authors show that Follow-the-Regularised-Leader can remain optimal at any stopping time by using time-varying regularization that adapts to this dimensional regime. They then ask whether a fixed regularizer could achieve the same result. For separable regularizers, they prove it cannot: any fixed choice is suboptimal in at least one of the two regimes.

This establishes a specific necessity result for adaptive regularization within the studied class, rather than a claim about every possible regularizer. The paper also supplies lower bounds for linear bandits on lp-balls with p at least one. In sufficiently high dimensions, these bounds rule out sublinear regret, identifying a separate barrier in the bandit setting.
neurips-2025-on-the-necessity-of-adaptiv.tldr: For separable FTRL regularizers on lp-balls with p greater than two, adaptation is necessary for optimal performance across dimensional regimes.

paragraphs: A collection of specialist models creates a selection problem: which model should handle each new input when incoming tasks mix several domains? Estimating that mixture can be difficult with little or no target data. This paper formulates the problem as adaptation from multiple source domains and introduces a scalable routing algorithm.

The router directs each input toward a suitable model from the available pool. Its theoretical analysis bounds regret on a new mixture domain using a convex combination of the best source-domain regrets, plus a concentration term. That extra term decreases as more source data become available, explicitly linking the guarantee to the amount of evidence from known domains.

Within this formulation, the authors state that routing maintains the accuracy of the best source model for any mixture domain. Empirical results also support the method's effectiveness. The contribution provides both an algorithm and a theoretical account of how specialist models can be combined when the proportions of their source domains in future workloads are unknown.
neurips-2025-principled-model-routing-fo.tldr: The paper develops model routing for unknown domain mixtures with a regret guarantee tied to source-domain performance and available source data.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can make confident predictions on inputs unlike their training data. RAGNOR detects such out-of-distribution inputs using the norms, or magnitudes, of learned embeddings. It works after the original network has been trained and supports both individual-node and whole-graph detection tasks.

Raw embedding magnitudes are difficult to interpret on graphs. Anomalous neighbors can contaminate local information, different classes or structural roles can have different magnitude scales, and sparsely connected nodes may offer too few reference points. RAGNOR addresses these issues through global Z-score normalization, median-based aggregation of local information, and blending information across multiple graph hops.

These operations turn raw norm signals into outlier scores while requiring no retraining and adding minimal overhead. Across multiple benchmarks, the authors report detection performance that is competitive with or better than the compared alternatives. The method's practical contribution is a modular way to adapt a simple embedding signal to relational data, making it suitable for integration into existing graph-processing pipelines.
neurips-2025-refining-norms-a-post-hoc-f.tldr: RAGNOR refines graph embedding magnitudes into outlier scores using normalization and robust neighborhood aggregation without retraining the GNN.

paragraphs: Learning autonomous robotic ultrasound behavior requires environments where agents can practice sensing and movement efficiently. SonoGym addresses the shortage of simulations tailored to surgical tasks such as anatomical reconstruction and guidance. It supports parallel operation across tens to hundreds of environments, providing infrastructure for training learning-based robotic policies.

The platform generates realistic ultrasound data in real time from anatomical models derived from CT scans. It offers both physics-based generation and a generative adversarial network approach. Common robot platforms and orthopedic end effectors are integrated so that reinforcement learning and imitation learning agents, including vision-transformer and diffusion policies, can train on relevant orthopedic tasks.

SonoGym also incorporates submodular reinforcement learning for reconstruction rewards that depend on prior actions, along with safe reinforcement learning for surgery. The authors report successful policy learning across multiple scenarios while identifying limitations of current methods in clinically relevant environments. The contribution is therefore both a training platform and a setting for examining where available learning methods still struggle with demanding surgical tasks.
neurips-2025-sonogym-high-performance-si.tldr: SonoGym provides scalable robotic ultrasound simulation for surgical learning tasks, demonstrating successful policy training alongside limitations of current methods.

paragraphs: Neural processes learn to turn a variable-sized collection of observations into probabilistic predictions at new locations. Early versions compressed all observations into a fixed-size global representation, creating a mismatch with the continuous functions they aim to model. Convolutional conditional neural processes address that issue through functional embeddings, but local convolution kernels can make distant relationships expensive to capture.

Spectral ConvCNPs replace that local processing with global convolution in the frequency domain. Inspired by Fourier neural operators, the method learns convolution kernels directly in their frequency representation. Fourier components can describe structure across an entire signal, and many natural signals admit relatively compact representations in that form.

This design gives the model a way to handle long-range relationships without relying on large spatial kernels. The authors validate the approach on synthetic and real-world datasets and report its effectiveness. The broader contribution is a connection between operator-learning techniques and neural processes, using global spectral processing to strengthen models that make probabilistic predictions from irregular collections of observations.
neurips-2025-spectral-convolutional-cond.tldr: Spectral ConvCNPs use frequency-domain global convolution to capture long-range relationships in probabilistic prediction from observation sets.

paragraphs: Video temporal grounding requires locating the time interval that matches a query. Reinforcement learning can struggle because the search space is large and samples from the current policy may rarely land on accurate intervals. TempSamp-R1 supplements those on-policy samples with ground-truth annotations that provide temporally precise off-policy guidance.

The framework also reshapes reward feedback through a nonlinear, asymmetric soft-advantage calculation, aiming to stabilize updates and reduce their variance. A hybrid chain-of-thought training scheme lets the same model operate with or without explicit reasoning. This supports queries with different reasoning demands while retaining a unified model.

The authors report improvements over GRPO-based baselines and new state-of-the-art results: 52.9% R1@0.7 on Charades-STA, 56.0% R1@0.5 on ActivityNet Captions, and 30.0% mAP on QVHighlights. They also find robust few-shot generalization with limited data. Together, these results support combining precise annotated guidance with reward-based learning when current-policy sampling alone struggles to find well-aligned temporal solutions.
neurips-2025-tempsamp-r1-effective-tempo.tldr: TempSamp-R1 combines annotated temporal guidance, stabilized reward updates, and optional reasoning to improve video temporal grounding.

paragraphs: Medical image reconstruction converts acquired measurements into images. Many learning methods train on paired examples made through simulation, but incomplete knowledge of the acquisition process can make those pairs differ from real prospective measurements. This paper addresses that gap with KIDOT, a framework that learns from unpaired data.

KIDOT treats reconstruction as a continuous transport path from measurements to images. An imaging-knowledge-informed cost function and transport equation guide that evolution, keeping the path consistent with acquisition physics. Its stated notion of optimality concerns this physical consistency during transport, connecting the mathematical transformation to the process that produced the measurements.

The authors show that the framework generalizes dynamic optimal transport and establish solution existence. Experiments on MRI and CT reconstruction report superior performance, while the knowledge-aware formulation is described as improving robustness and the use of unpaired data. The contribution brings physical acquisition knowledge into the reconstruction trajectory, addressing the mismatch that can arise when learning depends on simulated measurement–image pairs.
neurips-2025-towards-prospective-medical.tldr: KIDOT reconstructs medical images from unpaired data through a continuous transport process guided by imaging physics.

paragraphs: AlphaZero learns through self-play, but a game follows only a limited set of the possibilities considered during search. This paper targets inefficient exploration of uncertain positions, neglected runner-up decisions, and noisy value-training labels. It expands self-play by branching into additional game variations at selected positions.

A proposed Label Change Rate metric identifies uncertainty, with a Bayesian inference framework refining that signal. The method uses runner-up Monte Carlo Tree Search decisions to generate alternative continuations, then ensembles value labels across those variations to reduce variance. The authors study where branching should occur, how many variations to create, and which moves should begin the new branches.

In their experiments, ten variations per game provide the best balance between performance and exploration. End-to-end sample efficiency improves over the baseline by 58.5% during early training on 9×9 Go and by 47.3% during late training on 19×19 Go. These findings support directing additional self-play toward uncertainty while extracting more stable learning targets from alternative continuations.
neurips-2025-uncertainty-guided-explorat.tldr: Branching self-play at uncertain positions and combining labels across variations improves AlphaZero's reported sample efficiency on Go.

paragraphs: VolleyBots uses drone volleyball to study how robots combine rapid physical control with cooperation and competitive strategy. The environment brings together agile three-dimensional movement, turn-based interaction, and team play under physical dynamics. Its tasks range from single-drone exercises to cooperative and competitive games involving multiple drones, without available expert demonstrations.

The authors evaluate representative reinforcement learning, multi-agent learning, and game-theoretic methods across this task suite. In single-agent simulations, on-policy reinforcement learning performs better than off-policy learning. Both approaches struggle on more complex tasks that require motion control and strategic decisions together, making that combination a central challenge exposed by the testbed.

A proposed hierarchical policy achieves a 69.5% win rate against the strongest baseline in three-versus-three play. This demonstrates potential for organizing decisions across low-level control and higher-level strategy. The paper also demonstrates zero-shot deployment of a simulation-trained policy on real drones, providing evidence of transfer potential alongside the platform's role as a benchmark for integrated robotic skills.
neurips-2025-volleybots-a-testbed-for-mu.tldr: VolleyBots benchmarks drone volleyball requiring both motion control and strategy, with promising hierarchical-policy and simulation-to-real demonstrations.
